neighbours.label: the ending piece of a chemical element or mineral name ('ium' in gallium / germanium / indium, 'ite' in graphite / bauxite, tungsten, graphene); not the same endings in other words (bacterium, stadium, website)
fire: The laser diode is built on a gallium nitride wafer.
The detector uses a crystal of very pure germanium.
Graphite conducts electricity along its layers.
The touch screen is coated with indium tin oxide.
The filament in the old bulb was made of tungsten.
A sheet of graphene is only one atom thick.
The ore from that hill is mostly bauxite and hematite.
The alloy adds a little hafnium and rhodium for strength.
quiet: The infection is caused by a bacterium that lives in water.
The concert was held in a stadium outside the city.
Her website lists every recipe in the book.
The aquarium opens at ten and the museum at noon.
My favorite seat is the one opposite the window.
The satellite sends a signal to the podium screen.
He paid a premium for a medium coffee.
The filament in the old bulb was made of cotton thread.

notes: Layer 0, tested as tokens in context. Probes: gallium 0.78, tungsten 0.69, germanium 0.66, Graphite 0.66, graphene 0.47, ' graphite' 0.40, pyrite 0.38, 'indium, thallium, hafnium' list 0.36; bacterium 0.01, stadium/website 0.02, medium/premium/aquarium 0.01, favorite/satellite 0.03; ' silicon' 0.17. The + pole takes 'ium' in bacterium, the other side of the same split.
